Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:10:1.hebrew: רבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית - שיהו לו ולדות ממנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:10:1.english: His master may provide him with a Canaanite maidservant - So that he will have children from her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:10:2.hebrew: אין רבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית - ואסורה לו. אבל במכרוהו ב"ד, כתיב (שמות כ״א:ד׳): אם אדוניו יתן לו אשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:10:2.english: His master may not provide him with a Canaanite maidservant - And she is forbidden to him. But in the case of one whom the court sold, it is written (Exodus 21:4): "If his master gives him a wife."

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:11:1.hebrew: לא יליף שכיר שכיר - הילכך, דלא כתיב ביה, לא כתיב ביה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:11:1.english: Does not derive “hired worker, hired worker” - Therefore, whatever is not written explicitly about [this slave] is simply not written about him, [and the laws stated about the other slave are not applied to him through a verbal analogy (gezerah shavah)].

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:12:1.hebrew: דכולי עלמא יליף שכיר שכיר - לשאר מילי. והני, לת"ק בהדיא כתיב מיעוטייהו, ולא אהני ליה גזירה שוה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:12:1.english: Everyone derives "hired worker" from "hired worker" - For other matters. And these [cases], according to the first Tanna, their exclusion is explicitly written, and the verbal analogy does not avail him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:13:1.hebrew: ולא ליורשין - דאינו עובד לא את הבת ולא את האח, אם אין לו בן. אבל עובד הוא את הבן, כדלקמן (קידושין דף יז:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:13:1.english: And not for heirs - For he does not serve either the daughter or the brother, if [the master] has no son. But he does serve the son, as [stated] below (Kiddushin 17b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:14:1.hebrew: ועבדך אחרינא כתיב - הכתוב "כי משנה שכר שכיר עבדך":
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:14:1.english: “And he shall serve you” is written another [time] - “For he has served you [at] double the wage of a hired servant” (Deuteronomy 15:18).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:14:2.hebrew: להרצאת אדון - להרצות על ידי הענקו, שלא יקשה בעיניו, כדמפרש קרא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:14:2.english: To appease the master - To appease [him] through giving him a parting gift, so that it not be difficult in his eyes, as the verse explains.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:15:1.hebrew: אזנו - מיעוט הוא, דקרא יתירא לדרשה, דהא כתיב "ונתת באזנו":
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:15:1.english: His ear - It is an exclusion, [for] the verse is superfluous for the purpose of the teaching, since it is [already] written, "and you shall put it through his ear."

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:1:1.hebrew: מסולייא - נפחת, כדמסיים ואזיל: שאין לו עקב — שול"א (סוליה) בלע"ז:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:1:1.english: Mesulayya - Damaged, as [the Gemara] goes on to conclude: "that has no heel" — sole (sole) in Old French.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:2:1.english: Is acquired through money or through a document - In the Gemara, it derives this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:2:2.english: Through years - At the end of six years, he goes free.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:2:3.english: And through the Jubilee - If the Jubilee occurs within the six [years].

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:2:4.hebrew: ובגרעון כסף - פודה את עצמו, ומגרע לו אדונו מפדיונו דמי שיעבוד השנים שעברו, והכל לפי חשבון דמי מקנתו, כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:נ׳): "והיה כסף ממכרו במספר שנים". קנאו בשש מנים ועתיד לצאת בסוף שש — נמצא קונה עבודת כל שנה במנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:2:4.english: And through the deduction of money - He redeems himself, and his master deducts from his redemption [payment] the value of the servitude of the years that have passed, and everything is according to the calculation of his purchase price, as it is written: “And the price of his sale shall be according to the number of years” (Leviticus 25:50). [For example, if the master] bought him for six manehs and he is destined to go free at the end of six [years], it turns out that [the master] purchases the labor of each year for one maneh.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:2:5.hebrew: יתירה עליו - שקונה עצמה בכל אלה ובסימני נערות, כדילפינן לעיל (קידושין דף ד.) מויצאה חנם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:2:5.english: More than him - In that she acquires herself through all these [modes], and through the signs of maidenhood, as we derived earlier (Kiddushin 4a) from: "And she shall go out for nothing" (Exodus 21:11).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:2:6.hebrew: ובמיתת האדון - ואינו עובד את יורשיו. אבל עבד הנמכר בתחילתו, ומת האדון בתוך שש — משלימן ליורשיו. וכולהו יליף בגמ':
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:2:6.english: Or through the death of the master - And he does not serve [the master's] heirs. But as for a slave who is sold initially, if the master dies within the six [years], he completes them for his heirs. And all of these are derived in the Gemara.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:3:1.hebrew: מכסף מקנתו - בעבד עברי הנמכר לעובד כוכבים הכתוב מדבר, "וכי תשיג יד גר ותושב":
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:3:1.english: Out of the money that he was bought for - The verse is speaking of a Hebrew slave who is sold to a gentile, [as it states]: “And if a stranger or sojourner [with you] becomes rich” (Leviticus 25:47).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:3:2.hebrew: הואיל וכל קנינו - של עובד כוכבים בכסף, שלא נאמרה בו משיכה במטלטלין, אלא בישראל כתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:י״ד) מיד עמיתך — עד שימשוך מיד ליד. לפיכך, עבד נקנה לו בכסף:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:3:2.english: Since all of his acquisitions - [Those] of a gentile [are] with money, for *meshikhah* [drawing] of movable property was not stated regarding him; rather, regarding an Israelite it is written (Leviticus 25:14): “From the hand of your fellow” — until he draws [it] from hand to hand. Therefore, a slave is acquired by him with money.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:4:1.hebrew: שמגרעת פדיונה - מדלא כתיב ונפדה, משמע והפדה — שאף הבעל מסייע בפדיונה. אלמא בכסף נקנה, דאי לא קנאה בדמים, מאי מגרעה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:4:1.english: That she deducts from her redemption - Since it is not written “and she shall be redeemed” [venifdah], “and he shall let her be redeemed” [vehefdah] implies that even the master assists in her redemption. It follows that [a Hebrew slave] is acquired with money, for if he did not acquire her with money, what would she deduct?

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:5:1.hebrew: אשכחן אמה העבריה דמקניא בכסף - והדין נותן, הואיל וקידושיה בכסף, קנינה בכסף:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:5:1.english: We found that a Hebrew maidservant is acquired with money - And logic dictates that since her betrothal is with money, her acquisition is with money.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:6:1.hebrew: מכרוהו ב"ד - בגניבתו, דכי ימכר ע"י אחרים משמע. והדין נותן שיהא נקנה בכסף בלא חזקה, הואיל ויש בו צד קל, שנמכר בעל כרחו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:6:1.english: [A slave whom] the court sold - [This refers to one sold] for his theft, for "if he is sold" implies [being sold] by others. And logic dictates that he should be acquired through money without [requiring] an act of possession [chazakah], since he has a lenient aspect, in that he is sold against his will.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:7:1.hebrew: שכיר שכיר - נאמר במוכר עצמו (שם): ״כי ימוך אחיך ונמכר וגו', כשכיר כתושב יהיה עמך״. ונאמר במכרוהו ב"ד: ״כי משנה שכר שכיר וגו'״ — בפרשת ״כי ימכר״ כתיב (דברים ט״ו:י״ח):
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:7:1.english: “Hired worker” [and] “hired worker” - It is stated with regard to one who sells himself (ibid.): “If your brother becomes impoverished and is sold...” etc., “as a hired worker and as a settler he shall be with you.” And it is stated with regard to one whom the court sold: “For double the hire of a hired worker...” etc. — it is written in the passage of “If [your brother] is sold” (Deuteronomy 15:18).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:7:2.hebrew: למאן דלא יליף - דלית ליה הך גזירה שוה, ולקמיה מפרש מאן ניהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:7:2.english: According to the one who does not derive - Who does not accept this verbal analogy, and later on [the Gemara] explains who it is.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:8:1.hebrew: וכי תשיג - במוכר עצמו לעובד כוכבים, וסמכוה לפרשת מוכר עצמו לישראל, וילמד נמכר לישראל מנמכר לעובד כוכבים בהיקישא. ובנמכר לעובד כוכבים כתיב: ״מכסף מקנתו״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:8:1.english: And if [a stranger...] becomes rich - [This refers to] one who sells himself to a gentile, and [Scripture] juxtaposed it to the section of one who sells himself to an Israelite, and let [the case of one] sold to an Israelite be derived from [one] sold to a gentile via juxtaposition [hekesh]. And regarding [one] sold to a gentile, it is written: “Out of the money with which he was bought” (Leviticus 25:51).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:9:1.english: And more than six [years] - If he stipulated to be sold for ten years.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:9:2.hebrew: מכרוהו ב"ד - דכתיב (שם) ועבדך שש שנים. אבל במוכר עצמו לא כתיב שש, דכי תקנה עבד עברי — מיד אחרים משמע. ורציעה במכרוהו ב"ד כתיבא, וכן הענקה, דגבי ״ימכר לך״ כתיבי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14b:9:2.english: The court sold him - For it is written (there), "and he shall serve you six years." But regarding one who sells himself, "six" is not written, for "When you acquire a Hebrew slave" implies [acquiring him] from others. And the piercing [of the ear] is written regarding one whom the court sold, and likewise the severance gift, for they are written in connection with "he shall be sold to you."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 14b:13:1.hebrew: לך ולא ליורש - פי' כגון בת ואח; אבל עובד הוא את הבן, כדלקמן (קידושין דף יז:):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 14b:13:1.english: "For you, and not for an heir" - Explanation: for example, a daughter or a brother; but he does serve the son, as [stated] below (Kiddushin 17b):

Tosafot on Kiddushin 14b:15:1.hebrew: ולא אזנו של מוכר עצמו - וא"ת: למ"ל אזנו למעוטי דמוכר עצמו אינו נרצע? תיפוק ליה דמוכר עצמו אינו נרצע, דאין רבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית, כדלקמן (קידושין דף כא:), דבעינן "אהבתי את אשתי ואת בני"! וי"ל: דאי לאו "אזנו" הוה ילפינן מג"ש דשכיר שכיר ממכרוהו ב"ד, דאף על גב דלא מצי אמר "אהבתי את אשתי" ה"א דנרצע; קמ"ל "אזנו" דאין נרצע:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 14b:15:1.english: “And not the ear of one who sells himself” - If you ask: Why is “his ear” needed to exclude one who sells himself from being pierced? Let it be derived [that he is not pierced] from the fact that his master may not give him a Canaanite maidservant, as [stated] below (Kiddushin 21b), since we require [the slave to say] “I love my wife and my children”! And one can answer: Were it not for [the word] “his ear,” we would derive [the law] by a verbal analogy of “hired worker” and “hired worker” from one sold by the court. [We would then say] that even though he cannot say “I love my wife,” one might have thought that he is pierced. Therefore the verse teaches us, “his ear,” that he is not pierced:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 14b:3:1.hebrew: הואיל וכל קנינו בכסף - פ"ה: הואיל ולא נאמר בו משיכה כישראל, דכתיב: "או קנה מיד עמיתך" — דבר הנקנה מיד ליד, דהיינו משיכה. וקשה לר"ת: לפי שיהא סתמא דגמרא כדר"ל?! דלר' יוחנן, דאמר בפ' הזהב (ב"מ דף מז:): "דבר תורה מעות קונות", דרשינן בפ"ב דבכורות (דף יג:): "מיד עמיתך" — בכסף, הא לעובד כוכבים — במשיכה, וקי"ל כר' יוחנן לגבי ריש לקיש! ועוד, דבמס' ע"ז (דף עב.) אמרינן דלכ"ע משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה! לכך נראה לר"ת דה"פ: הואיל וכל קניינו דעובד כוכבים בעבד עברי בכסף, דכתיב ביה: "מכסף מקנתו" — לאפוקי שאינו קונה בשטר; דישראל גופיה לא קני ע"ע בשטר אלא משום דאיתקש לאמה, ואמה לאחרת, דדרשינן (לקמן קידושין דף טז.): "מה אחרת מקניא בשטר אף זו וכו'", ובעובד כוכבים לא שייך האי טעמא, שהרי אינו בתורת גיטין וקידושין. ועוד נראה לר"ת, דאפילו בקרקעות עובד כוכבים אינו קונה בשטר, כדאמר בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף נד.): "עובד כוכבים מכי מטא זוזי לידיה איסתלק ליה, וישראל לא קני עד דמטא שטרא לידיה" — משמע דאין קנין שטר לעובד כוכבים. וא"ת: לאו ק"ו הוא?! ומה עובד כוכבים שאינו קונה ע"ע בשטר — קונה בכסף, ישראל כו'?! וי"ל: דמסתברא דלכל אחד יש קנין לעצמו, כדאשכחן בפ"ב דבכורות (דף יג:) גבי מטלטלין: מדישראל בחדא, עובד כוכבים נמי בחדא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 14b:3:1.english: "Since all of his acquisition is with money" - Rashi explains: Since meshikhah was not stated regarding him [a gentile] as [it was] regarding an Israelite, as it is written: "Or acquire from the hand of your fellow" (Leviticus 25:14) — [implying] an item that is acquired from hand to hand, which is meshikhah. And Rabbeinu Tam found this difficult: For [according to this,] would the anonymous Gemara follow Reish Lakish?! For according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said in the chapter [entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 47b): "By Torah law, money acquires," we expound in the second chapter of Bekhorot (13b): "From the hand of your fellow" — with money, but [from/for] a gentile — through meshikhah; and we rule in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan over Reish Lakish! And furthermore, in Tractate Avodah Zarah (72a) we say that according to all opinions, meshikhah by a gentile acquires! Therefore, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that this is the explanation: "Since all of his acquisition" — [that] of a gentile regarding a Hebrew slave — "is with money," for it is written regarding him: "Out of the money of his purchase" (Leviticus 25:51), to exclude [the possibility] that he acquires through a deed; for an Israelite himself does not acquire a Hebrew slave through a deed except because he is compared to a [Hebrew] maidservant, and a maidservant to "another [woman]," as we expound (below, Kiddushin 16a): "Just as another [woman] is acquired through a deed, so too this one, etc."; and regarding a gentile, this reasoning does not apply, since he is not subject to the laws of divorce and betrothal. And furthermore, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that even regarding land, a gentile does not acquire through a deed, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Chezkas HaBatim (Bava Batra 54b): "A gentile, as soon as the money reaches his hand, withdraws [his ownership], and an Israelite does not acquire until the deed reaches his hand" — which implies that there is no acquisition via a deed for a gentile. And if you say: Is this not an a fortiori argument [kal va-chomer]: If a gentile, who does not acquire a Hebrew slave through a deed, acquires [him] with money, [should not an] Israelite, [who does acquire him through a deed, all the more so acquire him with money]?! And one can answer that it is logical that each has a mode of acquisition to himself, as we find in the second chapter of Bekhorot (13b) regarding movables: Since an Israelite [acquires] through one [mode], a gentile also [acquires] through one [mode].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 14b:6:1.hebrew: מוכר עצמו מנ"ל יליף שכיר שכיר - פי' בקונטרס: נאמר במוכר עצמו "כשכיר כתושב יהיה עמך", ונאמר במכרוהו ב"ד "כי משנה שכר שכיר". וא"ת: כיון דיליף "שכיר" "שכיר", למה איצטריך "מכסף מקנתו" גבי עובד כוכבים? נילף "שכיר" דכתיב גבי עובד כוכבים (ויקרא כ״ה:נ״ג) "כשכיר שנה בשנה וגו'" מנמכר לישראל, ונמכר לישראל מאמה, כדמפרש גמ' לעיל! וי"ל: דאיצטריך ליה לכדדרשינן לעיל (קידושין דף ח.): בכסף הוא נקנה, ואינו נקנה בתבואה וכלים. וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך "והפדה" לענין כסף? לישתוק מיניה, ונילף עבריה מע"ע הנמכר לישראל, ועברי הנמכר לישראל מעברי הנמכר לעובד כוכבים מג"ש ד"שכיר" "שכיר"! וי"ל: אה"נ, אלא איצטריך לדרשה אחרינא — לגרעון כסף. וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך היקישא דע"ע ועבריה לקנין כסף? נילף "שכיר" "שכיר" מנמכר לעובד כוכבים! וי"ל: דהיקישא דע"ע לעבריה איצטריך למימר: מה עבריה אינה יוצאה בראשי איברים — אף עברי אינו יוצא, ומה עברי יוצא בשש ויובל — אף עבריה כו':
Tosafot on Kiddushin 14b:6:1.english: "From where do we derive [that] one who sells himself [is acquired through money]? He derives [it from] 'hired worker' [and] 'hired worker'" - Rashi explained: It is stated regarding one who sells himself, "As a hired worker, as a settler he shall be with you" (Leviticus 25:40), and it is stated regarding one sold by the court, "For double of the hire of a hired worker [he has served you six years]" (Deuteronomy 15:18). And if you say: Since one derives [this through the verbal analogy of] "hired worker" [and] "hired worker," why was "out of the money that he was bought for" needed regarding [a Hebrew slave sold to] a gentile? Let us derive [it through] "hired worker" written regarding [one sold to] a gentile (Leviticus 25:53), "as a hired worker year by year, etc.," from [one] sold to an Israelite, and [one] sold to an Israelite [is derived] from [a Hebrew] maidservant, as the Gemara explained above! And one can say: It was needed for that which we derived above (Kiddushin 8a): With money he is acquired, but he is not acquired with produce or utensils. And if you say: Why was "then he shall let her be redeemed" needed regarding the matter of money? Let [the verse] be silent concerning it, and let us derive a Hebrew maidservant from a Hebrew slave sold to an Israelite, and a Hebrew [slave] sold to an Israelite from a Hebrew [slave] sold to a gentile through the verbal analogy of "hired worker" [and] "hired worker"! And one can say: Indeed so; rather, it was needed for another derivation — for the deduction of money. And if you say: Why was the juxtaposition of a Hebrew slave and a Hebrew maidservant needed for acquisition through money? Let us derive [it through] "hired worker" [and] "hired worker" from [one] sold to a gentile! And one can say: The juxtaposition of a Hebrew slave to a Hebrew maidservant was needed to say: Just as a Hebrew maidservant does not go free for [the loss of] primary limbs, so too a Hebrew slave does not go free [for primary limbs]; and just as a Hebrew slave goes free after six [years] and in the Jubilee, so too a Hebrew maidservant, etc.
